sourceNotification: GSR 202(E), dated 7th March 2011, made under section 52(1)/(2)(j)/(2)(q) of the Legal Metrology Act, 2009 (1 of 2010)
extractedFromFile: 9 The Legal Metrology (Package Commodities) Rules, 2011.pdf (43 pages, supplied by the user)
extractionMethod: Full text extracted with pypdf and read in its entirety by the assistant; every rule below is transcribed/paraphrased from that text, not from model memory of a later-amended version of these rules.
disclaimer: This registry is a structuring of the 2011 Rules AS SUPPLIED. Where the source document itself notes that a proviso 'will stand withdrawn' or 'will stand amended' by a later GSR notification, that note is preserved verbatim in `amendmentNotes` and the ORIGINAL 2011 text is what is registered as `currentText` -- this file does not silently apply the later amendment, because the amending notification itself was not supplied. A human legal reviewer must confirm which version is in force for the jurisdiction/date of an inspection before this registry is treated as authoritative for enforcement.

checkTypeLegend.REQUIRED_DECLARATION: A specific declaration must appear on the package; absence is a breach.
checkTypeLegend.PATTERN_MATCH: A declaration must be present and in a specific format.
checkTypeLegend.TEXT_LEGIBILITY: A declaration must be legible/prominent/conspicuous -- a visual quality judgement.
checkTypeLegend.TEXT_HEIGHT: A minimum numeral/letter height applies -- requires physical calibration to verify from a photo.
checkTypeLegend.PLACEMENT_CHECK: Where on the package (principal display panel, spacing around numerals) the declaration must sit.
checkTypeLegend.PACKAGE_CONTEXT: Determines whether a rule/chapter applies at all (package type, size, consumer type).
checkTypeLegend.QUANTITY_THRESHOLD: A numeric quantity is compared against a schedule-defined threshold.
checkTypeLegend.STANDARD_PACK_SIZE: A commodity's pack size must be one of the sizes fixed by the Second Schedule.
checkTypeLegend.SCHEDULE_LOOKUP: Resolving the rule requires looking up a value in one of the seven Schedules.
checkTypeLegend.PHYSICAL_TEST_REQUIRED: Can only be verified by opening/weighing/measuring the physical package.
checkTypeLegend.EXTERNAL_DATA_REQUIRED: Requires information not on the package itself (e.g. a tax notification, a registration record, a price revision notice).
checkTypeLegend.PROCEDURAL: Governs an inspector's, dealer's or manufacturer's conduct/process, not a fact printed on a package.
checkTypeLegend.PENALTY_PROVISION: Defines a penalty; not a checkable declaration.
checkTypeLegend.DEFINITIONAL: Defines a term used elsewhere; not independently checkable.
checkTypeLegend.HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED: Requires a judgement call (deceptive design intent, genuineness of a relaxation request, etc.) that must go to a human inspector.

terms.meaning: A person/firm carrying on the business of buying, selling, supplying or distributing a packaged commodity, including a commission agent; excludes a manufacturer selling its own packaged commodity except when sold to someone other than a dealer.
For stored packages: the total number stored. For packages at/on the packing line: the maximum hourly output.
A person/firm who produces, makes or manufactures the commodity, OR who puts a mark on a package claiming it as their own product even if made by someone else.
An error in deficiency in the quantity of an individual package that does not exceed the limits in the First Schedule.
The quantity by weight, measure or number of the commodity in the package, excluding packaging/wrapper.
A person/firm who pre-packs a commodity, in any container, in units suitable for wholesale or retail sale.
The surface area of the package where the required information is grouped together (either all of it, or pre-printed and on-line information grouped separately).
The quantity by weight, measure or number of the commodity in the package.
A dealer who sells directly to the consumer; includes a wholesale dealer making such a direct sale.
A package intended for retail sale to the ultimate consumer for consumption, including imported packages. Proviso: 'ultimate consumer' excludes industrial or institutional consumers.
Sale/distribution/delivery of a commodity through retail shops/agencies for consumption by an individual or group.

The maximum price at which the packaged commodity may be sold to the consumer, printed as 'Maximum or Max. retail price Rs/-...inclusive of all taxes' or 'MRP Rs/-...incl. of all taxes', with paise rounding rules (below 50 paise rounds down to the preceding rupee; 50-95 paise rounds to the nearest 50 paise).
A Schedule appended to these rules.
A package containing the specified quantity of a commodity (per the Second Schedule).
A dealer who does not sell directly to a consumer but distributes/sells through intermediaries.

A package containing a number of retail packages not intended for sale to a single consumer directly, OR a bulk commodity sold to an intermediary for onward sale in smaller quantities, OR a package of ten or more labeled retail packages.

rules.title: Short title and Commencement
rules.currentText: These rules may be called The Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011. They came into force on 1 April 2011.

rules.title: Definitions
rules.currentText: See `definitions` block above.

rules.chapter: II - Provisions applicable to packages intended for retail sale
rules.title: Applicability of the Chapter
rules.currentText: Chapter II does NOT apply to: (a) packages of commodities containing more than 25 kg or 25 litre, excluding cement and fertilizer sold in bags up to 50 kg; and (b) packaged commodities meant for industrial or institutional consumers.
explanations: 'institutional consumer' = an institution (transportation, airways, railways, hotels, hospitals or other service institutions) that buys packaged commodities directly from the manufacturer for its own use.
'industrial consumer' = an industry that buys packaged commodities directly from the manufacturer for use by that industry.
exemptions: Quantity > 25 kg or 25 L (except cement/fertilizer bags up to 50 kg)
rules.notes: Net quantity (image/OCR-derived) can flag the >25kg/25L exemption automatically. Whether a specific package is destined for an industrial/institutional consumer generally cannot be determined from the package image alone and needs inspector context (who is it being sold to, at what premises).

rules.title: Regulation for pre-packing and sale of commodities in packaged form
rules.currentText: No person shall pre-pack, or cause/permit to be pre-packed, any commodity for sale, distribution or delivery unless the package bears, or has securely affixed, the declarations required under these rules.
explanations: Packages without the retail-sale-price declaration while still within the manufacturer's own premises are not a violation, provided every package leaving the premises for its destination carries the RSP declaration.

rules.title: Specific commodities to be packed and sold in recommended standard packages
rules.currentText: Commodities listed in the Second Schedule must be packed in the standard quantities specified there.

provisos.text: If a Second-Schedule commodity is packed in a size other than the prescribed one, the label must prominently declare 'Not a standard pack size under the Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011' or 'non standard size under the Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011'.
provisos.amendmentNote: The source document notes this proviso 'will stand withdrawn wef 01.07.2012 vide GSR 748(E) dated 24.10.2011'. That amending notification was NOT supplied to this system, so its exact replacement text is not registered here; a human reviewer must confirm current status for any inspection dated after 2012-07-01.

rules.title: Declaration: name and address of manufacturer/packer/importer
rules.currentText: The name and address of the manufacturer must be declared; where the manufacturer is not the packer, the name and address of both manufacturer and packer; for an imported package, the name and address of the importer must also be mentioned.
explanations: Explanation I: a name/address given without 'manufactured by' or 'packed by' is presumed to be the manufacturer's, and liability follows accordingly.

Explanation II: if a brand owner's name/address appears as a marketer, the brand owner is held responsible for violations (the deemed manufacturer); where more than one name/address appears, prosecution proceeds against whichever is listed first.
Explanation III: for food articles, this sub-rule does NOT apply -- the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and its rules apply instead.
exceptions: Food articles are governed by the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, not this sub-rule.
rules.applicability: Chapter II packages, excluding food articles (see Explanation III)

rules.title: Declaration: common/generic name of the commodity
rules.currentText: The common or generic name of the commodity must be declared; for packages with more than one product, the name and number/quantity of each product must be mentioned.

rules.title: Declaration: net quantity
rules.currentText: The net quantity, in standard units of weight or measure, must be declared; where sold by number, the number of the commodity in the package.

rules.title: Declaration: month and year of manufacture/pre-packing/import
rules.currentText: The month and year in which the commodity was manufactured, pre-packed or imported must be declared.

provisos.text: For food articles, the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and its rules apply instead.
Does not apply to packages of seeds labeled/certified under the Seeds Act, 1966.
A manufacturer may indicate the month/year using a rubber stamp without overwriting.
provisos.amendmentNote: Source document notes this proviso 'will stand withdrawn wef 01.07.2012 vide GSR 748(E) dated 24.10.2011'.

provisos.text: For cosmetics, the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945 apply.

exceptions: No month/year declaration required on: (i) packages of bidis or incense sticks; (ii) domestic LPG cylinders of 14.2kg or 5kg marketed by a public sector undertaking.
rules.applicability: Chapter II packages, excluding food articles, certified seeds, bidis/incense sticks, and specified LPG cylinders

rules.title: Declaration: retail sale price (MRP)
rules.currentText: The retail sale price of the package must be declared.

provisos.text: For alcoholic beverages/spirituous liquor, State Excise Laws apply within the manufacturing State; these rules only apply where the State law does not itself require an RSP declaration.

rules.title: Declaration: dimensions, where relevant
rules.currentText: Where the sizes of the commodity in the package are relevant, the dimensions must be declared; if pieces differ in size, each different piece's dimensions must be declared.
rules.applicability: Only commodities where size/dimension is relevant to the sale (e.g. bed-sheets, pipes, cables -- see also Rules 14-17)
rules.notes: Whether dimensions are 'relevant' for a given commodity category is a product-category judgement, not purely an image read.

rules.title: Declaration: such other matters as are specified in these rules
rules.currentText: A catch-all requiring whatever other declarations these rules specify elsewhere.

provisos.text: (A) No month/year-of-manufacture declaration required on bidi/incense-stick packages, or on 14.2kg/5kg public-sector-marketed domestic LPG cylinders.

(B) Packaging material pre-printed with a month may still be used into the next month if not exhausted (subject to Central Government extension in special circumstances); this does not apply to food products with a 'best before/use before' period of 90 days or less from manufacture/packing.
(C) No retail-sale-price declaration required on: (i) bidi packages; (ii) domestic LPG cylinders priced under the Administrative Price Mechanism.

explanations: Explanation I: the month/year may be expressed in words, numerals, or both.
rules.applicability: Chapter II packages, subject to the listed provisos

rules.title: Declaration: consumer-complaint contact
rules.currentText: Every package must bear the name, address, telephone number, and e-mail address (if available) of the person/office that can be contacted for consumer complaints.

rules.title: No individual stickers to alter/make required declarations
rules.currentText: It is not permissible to affix individual stickers to alter or make a declaration required under these rules.

provisos.text: A sticker MAY be used to reduce the MRP (inclusive of all taxes), provided it does not cover the manufacturer's/packer's original MRP declaration.

rules.notes: Detecting a sticker overlay (vs. printed text) reliably from a single photo is a vision-model inference at best, not a deterministic OCR check.

rules.title: Stickers permitted for non-required declarations
rules.currentText: Stickers may be used for declarations other than those required under these rules.

rules.title: Multi-component commodities packed in multiple units
rules.currentText: Where a commodity has multiple components packed in two or more units for sale as a single commodity, the Rule 6(1) declarations must appear on the main package (with the main package also noting the accompanying packages), or on each individual package with intimation on the main package; if sold as spare parts, all declarations must appear on each package.
rules.applicability: Multi-component commodities packed as one sale unit

rules.title: Exhaustion of old packaging material
rules.currentText: Packaging material/wrapper that could not be exhausted may be used up to 31 March 2012 (or until exhausted, whichever is earlier), after making corrections required under these rules by stamping, sticker, or on-line printing.
rules.amendmentNote: Source document notes the time was extended vide GSR 734(E) dated 30.09.2011; this is a time-bound transitional provision from the 2011 commencement and is not relevant to current-day inspections.

rules.title: Principal display panel for very small packages
rules.currentText: For a package of capacity 5 cubic cm or less, the principal display panel may be a card or tape firmly affixed to the package, bearing the required information.
rules.notes: Capacity in cubic cm cannot be reliably derived from a 2D photo without a calibration reference.

rules.title: Minimum numeral/letter height on the principal display panel
rules.currentText: The height of any numeral in the required declarations must not be less than the value in Table-I (net quantity by weight/volume) or Table-II (net quantity by length/area/number), by quantity band. Letters generally must be >=1mm high (>=2mm if blown/formed/molded/embossed/perforated); numeral/letter width must be >= 1/3 of height, except for '1' and the letters i, I, l.
rules.schedule_ref: TABLE_I_TABLE_II (embedded in Rule 7, not a numbered Schedule)
rules.notes: Explicitly NOT_ASSESSABLE_FROM_IMAGE without a calibration reference of known physical size in the same photo (a coin, a ruler, a printed scale bar). No such mechanism exists in this system. A future version could accept a reference object or a package of known standard dimensions to calibrate px-per-mm, but that is out of scope here.

rules.title: Exemption where another law already requires the same information
rules.currentText: Rule 7(1)-(3) do not apply to a package if the same information is already required to be given under some other law in force.

rules.title: Declarations must appear on the principal display panel; clear space around the quantity
rules.currentText: Every required declaration must appear on the principal display panel. The area around the quantity declaration must be free of other printed information: above/below by at least the numeral height, and left/right by at least twice the numeral height.
rules.notes: A vision model can plausibly flag 'this quantity declaration looks visually crowded' as an advisory signal, but precise multiples of numeral height require the same calibration problem as Rule 7.

rules.title: Returnable-bottle beverages: RSP on crown cap or bottle
rules.currentText: For soft drinks/ready-to-serve fruit beverages in a returnable, refillable bottle, the RSP may be shown on the crown cap or the bottle (or both); 'MRP Rs....' is sufficient in that case.

rules.title: Manner of declaration: legible, prominent, contrasting
rules.currentText: Every required declaration must be legible and prominent. Numerals of the RSP and net-quantity declarations must be printed/painted/inscribed in a colour that contrasts conspicuously with the label background.

provisos.text: Information blown/formed/molded on glass or plastic need not be in a contrasting colour.
Hand-written/hand-scripted declarations must be clear, unambiguous and legible.

rules.notes: OCR confidence is a reasonable proxy signal for legibility, but a formal contrast-ratio judgement needs controlled lighting/calibration this system does not have; treat as advisory, human-reviewed.

rules.title: Declaration must not require reading through liquid contents
rules.currentText: No declaration may be made so that it must be read through a liquid commodity in the package.

rules.title: Outer container/wrapper must repeat declarations
rules.currentText: An outer container/wrapper must also carry all required declarations, unless it is transparent and the inner package's declarations are easily readable through it.

provisos.text: No declaration is required on the inner package if the inner package's own outer cover carries none.

rules.applicability: Packages sold with an outer container/wrapper

rules.title: Language of declarations
rules.currentText: Required declarations must be in Hindi (Devanagari script) or English.

provisos.text: Another language may additionally be used alongside Hindi/English.

rules.notes: This OCR pipeline is tuned for English; a Devanagari-only label would need a second OCR pass this system does not currently run, and is flagged INCONCLUSIVE rather than treated as a language violation.

rules.title: Declaration of name and address of manufacturer, etc. -- detail
rules.currentText: Every package kept/offered/exposed for sale or sold must conspicuously bear the manufacturer's (or manufacturer + packer's) name and complete address; for imported packages, the importer's name and address. The name must be the actual corporate name or the name under which the business is conducted.

provisos.text: For packages of capacity <=5 cubic cm, a mark/inscription enabling identification of the manufacturer/packer/importer is sufficient.
Where a commodity manufactured outside India is packed in India, the principal display panel must also show the name and complete address of the Indian packer or importer.

explanations: 'complete address' = the factory's postal address, or (otherwise) street name, premises number if any, and city/State or PIN code sufficient to identify and locate the manufacturer/packer/importer.

rules.title: General provisions relating to declaration of quantity
rules.currentText: Wrapper/packaging weight is excluded from net quantity. Where quantity does not vary with environment, the declared quantity must equal what the consumer actually receives, and must not be qualified by 'when packed' or similar. Where quantity is likely to undergo negligible environmental variation, the declaration must account for that variation so the consumer receives not less than the declared quantity (also not qualified by 'when packed'). Where variation is significant, the declaration MAY be qualified by 'when packed', for the commodities listed in the Third Schedule.
rules.notes: Verifying actual received quantity vs. declared quantity is inherently a physical weighing/measuring exercise (see Rules 19-22 and the Fifth/Sixth Schedule), not an image check.

rules.title: Manner in which declaration of quantity shall be made
rules.currentText: Quantity must be expressed in a unit (or combination) giving accurate, adequate information: mass (solid/semi-solid/viscous/mixed), length (linear-measure sale), area (area-measure sale), volume (liquid/cubic-measure sale), or number (sold by number) -- except for commodities in the Fourth Schedule, which follow that Schedule's unit instead. An additional number-of-units declaration is optional when quantity is by mass. Where weight/measure/number alone isn't enough information, dimensions must also be declared. Additional information needed by the consumer must appear on the same panel as the other required declarations. The quantity declaration must not use exaggerating/misleading/inadequate words ('minimum', 'not less than', 'average', 'about', 'approximately' or similar). For packages of capacity <=5 cubic cm, the quantity declaration goes on a tag/card/tape/similar device that cannot be removed without opening the container, and it must also identify the manufacturer/packer.
rules.amendmentNote: Sub-rule (6)'s wording is noted in the source document as amended wef 01.07.2012 vide GSR 748(E) dated 24.10.2011 to a broader form ('any word or expression of any sort, whatsoever...'); the ORIGINAL 2011 wording is registered as currentText per this registry's policy (see top-level disclaimer).

rules.title: Statement of units of weight, measure or number
rules.currentText: Below 1 kg/1 m/1 sq.m/1 cubic m/1 cubic dm/1 L, the sub-multiple unit (gram, centimetre, sq. decimetre, cubic centimetre, cubic centimetre, millilitre respectively) must be used. At or above those thresholds, the base unit (kilogram, metre, sq. metre, cubic metre, litre) is used, with fractions expressed as decimals or sub-multiples (a proviso allows expressing an exact 1kg/1m/1sq.m/1 cubic dm/1 cubic m/1 L quantity in the smaller unit at the packer's option). No 'dozen', 'score', 'gross', 'great gross' or similar counting words may be used. Only SI units may be used for net quantity; items sold by number use the symbol 'N' or 'U'.

rules.title: Declarations for dimensioned textile-type commodities
rules.currentText: For bed-sheets, hemmed fabric, dhoties, sarees, napkins, pillow-covers, towels, table cloths and similar commodities, the number and finished dimensions must be declared.

provisos.text: If pieces of different dimensions are packed together, the dimensions and retail sale price of each piece must also be declared.
The dimensions and sale price of the commodity must also be marked on each individual piece.

rules.applicability: Bed-sheets, fabric, dhoties, sarees, napkins, pillow-covers, towels, table cloths and similar goods
rules.notes: Applicability depends on product-category classification.

rules.title: Declaration of dimensions/weight where they affect price
rules.currentText: Where dimensions and/or weight relate to the commodity's price, the quantity declaration must also include those dimensions/weight/combination.

rules.title: Declaration of number of usable sheets
rules.currentText: For packages of sheet-form commodities (aluminium foil, facial tissues, waxed paper, toilet paper and similar), the number of usable sheets and the dimensions of each sheet must be declared.
rules.applicability: Sheet-form commodities (foil, tissue, wax paper, toilet paper, etc.)

rules.title: Declarations for container-type commodities
rules.currentText: For bags, boxes, cups, pans and similar retail containers: (i) bag-type: number of bags + linear dimensions; (ii) square/oblong/rectangular containers: number + length, width, and (if required) depth; (iii) circular/round containers: number + diameter and (if necessary) depth; (iv) where capacity is referenced by label to a standard weight/measure, that reference must be included in the quantity declaration.
rules.applicability: Bags, boxes, cups, pans and similar containers sold as containers for other materials

rules.title: Wholesale/retail dealers must not sell non-compliant packages
rules.currentText: No wholesale dealer, retail dealer or importer shall sell, distribute, deliver, display or store for sale any packaged commodity unless it complies in all respects with the Act and these rules.
rules.applicability: Chapter II packages, at the point of dealer sale/display/storage
rules.notes: This is the umbrella obligation; it is operationalised by the specific declaration rules above (6, 7-17) rather than checked independently.

rules.title: No sale above declared retail sale price
rules.currentText: No retail dealer or other person (including manufacturer, packer, importer, wholesale dealer) may sell a packaged commodity above its declared retail sale price.
rules.notes: Requires the actual transacted sale price, which is not visible on the package image itself -- needs a receipt/observed transaction.

rules.title: Tax revision -> revised price procedure
rules.currentText: If tax on a pre-packed commodity is revised after packing, the dealer must not sell above the revised price communicated by the manufacturer/packer; the manufacturer/packer must publish the revised price via >=2 newspaper advertisements plus circulation of notices to dealers and to the Director/Controllers of Legal Metrology; the price difference charged must not exceed the actual tax change. Sub-rule (4): none of this applies to a package that is not required to carry a month/year-of-pre-packing declaration.

provisos.text: No newspaper publication needed if the revision is due to a State Legislature tax change.
Revised prices may only be charged on packages marked as pre-packed in the month of the tax change (or the following month).
Where the revised price is LOWER, the dealer must not charge more than the revised (lower) price, regardless of the month pre-packed.

rules.applicability: Packages affected by a post-packing tax revision
rules.notes: Requires the tax-revision notice and manufacturer's advertisement/circular, external to the package image.

rules.title: No obliterating/altering the printed retail sale price
rules.currentText: No wholesale/retail dealer or other person may obliterate, smudge or alter the RSP indicated by the manufacturer/packer/importer. The manufacturer/packer/importer itself must not alter the price on a wrapper once printed and used for packing.
rules.notes: OCR/vision can flag visible tampering/obliteration signals but this is fundamentally a human-inspector judgement of intent/alteration.

rules.title: VAT/TOT retailers must maintain a calibrated weighing machine
rules.currentText: Retailers registered for VAT/TOT and dealing in commodities declared by weight/volume must maintain an electronic weighing machine of at least accuracy class III (smallest division >=1g), with a printed-receipt facility showing gross quantity, price etc., available free of cost to consumers at the retail premises.
rules.notes: An on-premises equipment inspection, not a package-image check.

rules.title: Inspection of quantity/error at manufacturer's or packer's premises
rules.currentText: An authorized Legal Metrology officer may examine packages/lots at the manufacturer's/packer's premises, draw samples per the Fifth Schedule, and test per the Sixth Schedule; record results on the Seventh Schedule form with signatures; report findings including any error in deficiency; if the statistical average is short or any package's deficiency exceeds the maximum permissible error, fresh tests may be requested (fee: Rs 2500) with the previously tested lot held pending resolution; a 100% check-and-sort obligation falls on the manufacturer/packer if any package fails; mandatory-declaration compliance is checked at factory or depot level; non-compliance can lead to seizure of five representative samples as evidence, releasing the rest once compliance is ensured.
rules.notes: This is the on-site sampling/weighing procedure itself -- fundamentally a physical inspection workflow, not an image-analysis task. LM-GUARD's package-photo pipeline cannot perform it; it belongs to the field-inspection module of a Legal Metrology authority, outside this codebase's current scope.

rules.title: Action on completion of inspection at manufacturer's/packer's premises
rules.currentText: If the Rule 19 report shows a quantity shortfall beyond the permissible error, or a missing required declaration, the officer seizes the sample packages as evidence and may initiate action under the Act, unless fresh tests under Rule 19(4) are still pending. Seized packages are disposed of per the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

rules.title: Inspection of quantity/error at wholesale/retail dealer premises
rules.currentText: Testing at a dealer's premises ordinarily happens only on: (i) a specific consumer complaint of short quantity; (ii) suspected tampering/pilferage/leakage; or (iii) an observed missing declaration. On testing, the officer verifies quantity against the declared amount and the maximum permissible error; if deficiency exceeds the permissible error, the package is seized and action taken -- UNLESS the package bears the 'when packed' legend and the officer is satisfied the deficiency is due to environmental conditions. If quantity conforms (or deficiency is within tolerance), the dealer may sell at the tested quantity's price. If declarations are missing, the officer may inquire into the package's source.
rules.applicability: Dealer-premises inspections, on complaint/suspicion/observed missing declaration

rules.title: Establishment of maximum permissible error
rules.currentText: The maximum permissible error is as set out in the First Schedule, accounting for: (a) unavoidable weighing/measuring/counting deviation in good packaging practice; (b) ordinary exposure to climate/transport/storage in good distribution practice; and (c) variation due to the nature of the packaging material/container. The Director/Controller determines which commodities may be qualified by 'when packed' and the reasonable environmental variation allowed.

rules.title: Deceptive packages
rules.currentText: If the quantity in a sample package matches its declared quantity but the package is 'deceptive' (designed to give an exaggerated/misleading impression of quantity, other than where bigger dimensions are justified for product protection or filling-machine requirements), the officer requires the manufacturer/packer to repack/re-label it; failure leads to seizure and punitive action, with safe custody as court evidence. Seized perishable commodities are disposed of per the rules under the Act.
rules.notes: A vision model can flag a package as 'visually appears larger than its contents would require' as an advisory signal only -- 'deceptive package' is explicitly a judgement call reserved to the officer under this rule, with a justification defence (protection/filling-machine requirements) that requires manufacturer input.

rules.chapter: III - Provisions applicable to wholesale packages
rules.title: Declarations on every wholesale package
rules.currentText: Every wholesale package must bear: (a) name and address of the manufacturer/importer, or the packer if the manufacturer/importer is not the packer; (b) the identity of the commodity; (c) the total number of retail packages contained, or the net quantity in standard units.

provisos.text: Does not apply if an equivalent declaration is already required on the wholesale package by another law in force.

rules.applicability: Wholesale packages (see definition of 'wholesale package' in Rule 2(r))
rules.notes: Applicability requires classifying the package as wholesale (per Rule 2(r)) rather than retail -- a package-context judgement.

rules.chapter: IV - Export and import of packaged commodities
rules.title: Restrictions on sale of export packages in India
rules.currentText: An export package cannot be sold in India unless the manufacturer/packer has re-packed or re-labeled it per Chapter II; if sold without re-packing/re-labeling, it is liable to seizure under the Act.
rules.applicability: Packages originally packed for export, later sold domestically
rules.notes: Whether a given package was originally an 'export package' is generally not determinable from the image alone.

rules.title: Exemption in respect of certain packages
rules.currentText: These rules do not apply to a package if: (a) net weight/measure is 10g or 10ml or less (sold by weight/measure); (b) it is a fast-food item packed by a restaurant/hotel/similar; (c) it contains scheduled or non-scheduled formulations covered by the Drugs (Price Control) Order, 1995 (under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955); (d) it is an agricultural farm produce package above 50 kg.

provisos.text: The MRP and net-quantity declarations must still be made on packages of 10g-20g or 10ml-20ml.
provisos.amendmentNote: Source document notes this proviso 'will stand withdrawn wef 01.07.2012 vide GSR 748(E) dated 24.10.2011'.

rules.applicability: GATES the entire ruleset for the listed exempt package classes
exemptions: Fast-food packed by a restaurant/hotel and the like
rules.notes: Net quantity is image/OCR-derivable and can auto-trigger the <=10g/10ml exemption check; the other three exemption classes (fast food, price-controlled drugs, bulk agricultural produce) need product-category classification beyond OCR.

rules.chapter: VI - Registration of manufacturers and packers
rules.title: Registration of manufacturers, packers and importers
rules.currentText: Every pre-packer/importer must apply (with a Rs 500 fee) to the Director/Controller for registration of name and complete address, within 90 days of commencing (or of these rules' commencement, if already pre-packing/importing). The application must state the applicant's name, premises address, and commodity/commodities. Alteration of the registration certificate costs a Rs 100 fee. The Director/Controller returns incomplete applications within 7 working days, or registers and issues a certificate if complete.
rules.notes: Requires the manufacturer's registration record, which is not on the package.

rules.title: Registration of a shorter address
rules.currentText: A manufacturer/packer may apply to register a shorter address in addition to the complete address; the Director/Controller may approve it after inquiry if it is sufficient for identification; once registered, the shorter address may be used on the label.

rules.title: Register of manufacturers and packers
rules.currentText: The Director/Controller maintains a register of registered manufacturers/packers, open to public inspection free of charge.

rules.title: Compilation and circulation of lists of manufacturers/packers
rules.currentText: The Director/Controller compiles a State-wise list of registered manufacturers/packers and circulates it to the relevant State Controller to enable sample-taking at the premises.

rules.title: Advertisements mentioning retail sale price
rules.currentText: An advertisement mentioning the RSP of a pre-packaged commodity must declare the net quantity/number of the commodity. The net-quantity font size in the advertisement must match the RSP's font size.
rules.notes: Out of scope for a package-image pipeline; would require analysing the advertisement, a different input entirely.

rules.title: Penalty for contravention
rules.currentText: Contravention of rules 27-31 (registration/advertisement rules): fine of Rs 4,000. Contravention of any other rule with no penalty specified elsewhere in the Act/rules: fine of Rs 2,000.
rules.notes: Penalty amounts are informational context for a human inspector's enforcement decision; LM-GUARD does not impose penalties.

rules.title: Power to relax
rules.currentText: The Central Government may, after verifying the genuineness of a compounding/Court decision, permit a manufacturer/packer to pack for sale for a reasonable period while relaxing one or more provisions, subject to specified corrective measures.

rules.title: Repeal and savings
rules.currentText: The Standards of Weights and Measures (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 1977 are repealed, without prejudice to past operations, accrued rights/liabilities/penalties, or pending investigations/proceedings/appeals under the old rules, which continue as if these rules had not been made (with equivalent continuity for registrations, approvals, licences and pending applications).
